title: Best BI tools for high query volume and usage spikes (2026): 9 tools compared on concurrency, caching, and cost
summary: Databricks, Sigma, and Looker push query spikes to an autoscaling warehouse; Power BI, Quick Sight, and Tableau absorb them in capacity. 9 BI tools compared.
body_markdown:
The BI tools that handle query spikes best in November 2026 are Databricks AI/BI, Sigma, and Looker, because they send every query to a warehouse that can add compute on demand, while Power BI, Amazon Quick Sight, and Tableau Cloud absorb spikes in their own in-memory engines and capacity limits. ThoughtSpot, Metabase, and Basedash also query live but leave elasticity to your warehouse or your own servers. The deciding question is not which tool “scales” but where the extra compute comes from during a spike, and who pays for it.


## How we evaluated BI tools for query spikes


We read each vendor’s official documentation and pricing pages on November 23, 2026, and compared nine tools on five criteria:


1. **Where queries run:** live against your warehouse, in the vendor’s in-memory engine, or both. This decides which system has to scale.
2. **Caching:** whether the tool caches results, the default cache lifetime, and whether a cache hit avoids running a warehouse query.
3. **Documented limits under load:** concurrency caps, queues, timeouts, and what happens when you hit them (queueing, throttling, rejection, or overage billing).
4. **How cost grows:** whether more viewers or more queries raise the bill, and whether you can forecast it.
5. **Security and AI at scale:** row-level security, SAML SSO, and SCIM for large user counts, plus how AI features are metered as question volume grows.


We didn’t run load tests. Every limit below is the vendor’s own published number.


## Where the extra compute comes from: your warehouse


For live-query BI tools, the warehouse does most of the scaling:


- **Snowflake:**[multi-cluster warehouses](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/warehouses-multicluster) are an Enterprise Edition feature. In auto-scale mode, “Snowflake starts and stops clusters as needed” between the minimum and maximum you set. Repeated identical queries can also hit the[24-hour result cache](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/querying-persisted-results) .
- **BigQuery:** on-demand queries cost $6.25 per TiB scanned after the first free TiB each month and get “up to 2,000 concurrent slots, shared among all queries in a single project” ([BigQuery pricing](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/pricing) ). Capacity reservations can use[autoscaling slots](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/slots-autoscaling-intro) , and[BI Engine](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/bi-engine-intro) caches frequently used data in memory.
- **Amazon Redshift:**[Concurrency Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/concurrency-scaling.html) adds cluster capacity automatically, and each cluster earns up to one free hour of it per day ([Redshift pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/redshift/pricing/) ).[Redshift Serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/serverless-capacity.html) scales between a base of 4 and 512 RPUs.
- **ClickHouse Cloud:** Scale and Enterprise tier services can[autoscale vertically](https://clickhouse.com/docs/manage/scaling) and scale horizontally through the console or API.


If your warehouse can’t add compute, a live-query BI tool will queue or time out during a spike. Our[playbook for cutting warehouse costs from BI dashboards](https://www.basedash.com/blog/how-to-cut-cloud-data-warehouse-costs-from-bi-dashboards) covers the warehouse-side settings in more depth.

## Databricks AI/BI: best when your data already lives in Databricks


**Best for:** teams on the Databricks lakehouse that want dashboards and AI chat without adding another vendor. **Not ideal for:** data that lives outside Databricks, or teams without someone to size SQL warehouses.


- **Pricing:** “There are no additional license fees to use AI/BI. Standard Databricks Lakehouse $DBU rates apply” ([Databricks AI/BI](https://www.databricks.com/product/business-intelligence) ). Serverless SQL warehouses bill a fixed DBU-per-hour rate by warehouse size. 14-day free trial. Verified November 2026.
- **Under load:** serverless warehouses use[Intelligent Workload Management](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/sql-warehouse/warehouse-behavior) . When capacity is full, queries queue and “the autoscaler quickly provisions more clusters.” The queue holds up to 1,000 queries. The default is one cluster minimum and maximum, and Databricks[recommends](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/compute/sql-warehouse/create) “a cluster for every 10 concurrent queries,” so raise the maximum before a known spike.
- **Caching:** dashboards keep a[24-hour result cache](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dashboards/caching) , and “serving results from the dashboard cache does not start the SQL warehouse.” Cached results can be up to 24 hours old.
- **Security:** Unity Catalog[row filters and column masks](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/filters-and-masks/) apply at query time. SCIM requires the Premium plan or above.
- **AI:**[Genie](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie/) answers questions in plain English. Each user gets 150 free DBUs per month, Genie One and Genie Agents usage is free until January 31, 2027, and the SQL compute Genie uses is billed separately ([Genie cost](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie/monitor-cost) ).
- **Embedding:** iframe embedding, including for external users without Databricks accounts ([embedding docs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dashboards/embedding/) ). Genie can’t be embedded for external users; use the Genie Conversation API instead.


## Sigma: best for spreadsheet-style exploration on an elastic warehouse


**Best for:** business users who want to explore Snowflake or BigQuery data in a spreadsheet interface without writing SQL. **Not ideal for:** teams that need a published price, or that want the BI tool to cap warehouse spend for them.


- **Pricing:** not public; Sigma sells View, Act, Analyze, and Build license tiers ([license overview](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/account-type-and-license-overview) ) and charges credits for billable events such as data inputs, exports, and, since November 1, 2026, messages to agents ([billable usage](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/about-billable-usage-events) ). 7-day free trial. Verified November 2026.
- **Under load:** “Sigma does not store your data” and runs its SQL in your warehouse ([caching and freshness](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/caching-and-data-freshness) ), so a multi-cluster Snowflake warehouse or BigQuery autoscaling does the scaling. For certain platforms, Sigma’s own queue limits concurrent requests ([query details](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/examine-workbook-queries) ), and queries time out after 120 seconds by default.
- **Caching:** the query ID cache lasts 10 minutes by default ([cache duration](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/set-a-query-id-cache-duration) ). The universal result cache is in beta and doesn’t support Snowflake or BigQuery.[Materializations](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/materialization) write a dataset back to your warehouse as a table, which cuts repeated heavy queries.
- **Security:** row-level and column-level security,[SAML SSO](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/single-sign-on-with-saml) , and SCIM.
- **AI:**[Sigma Assistant](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/ask-natural-language-queries-with-assistant) is a natural language query interface, included from the View tier.
- **Embedding:** JWT-signed iframes and a React embed SDK, sold as a premium feature.


For a direct comparison, see[Basedash vs Sigma](https://www.basedash.com/vs/basedash-vs-sigma) .


## Looker: best for governed metrics at large user counts


**Best for:** enterprises that want one modeled definition of every metric and fine control over how many queries hit the warehouse. **Not ideal for:** small teams that want a published price or don’t want to maintain LookML.


- **Pricing:** quote only, as a platform fee plus Developer, Standard, and Viewer user licenses ([Looker pricing](https://cloud.google.com/looker/pricing) ). The Standard edition is for “fewer than 50 users” and includes up to 1,000 query-based API calls per month; Enterprise includes 100,000 and Embed 500,000. Trial instances last 90 days. Verified November 2026.
- **Under load:** the “Max connections per node” setting caps “the number of simultaneous queries that Looker can run against your database.” Beyond that, “Looker will queue them internally and process them in order,” and a per-user concurrent query cap is “commonly 25” ([connection settings](https://cloud.google.com/looker/docs/connecting-to-your-db) ). A spike shows up as wait time rather than warehouse cost.
- **Caching:** “The default cache retention policy is one hour,” and[datagroups](https://cloud.google.com/looker/docs/caching-and-datagroups) tie cache and persistent derived table rebuilds to your ETL schedule.[Aggregate awareness](https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/aggregate_awareness) routes queries to the smallest pre-aggregated table available.
- **Security:** access filters for row-level security, SAML and OpenID Connect, and SCIM in Preview through Workforce Identity Federation.
- **AI:** Conversational Analytics and Gemini in Looker are free without allocation limits through January 31, 2027. From February 1, 2027, overage is billed at $3.00 per million input tokens and $20.00 per million output tokens.
- **Embedding:** private embedding on every edition; signed and cookieless embedding only on the Embed edition.


## Power BI: best for Microsoft shops that can size a capacity


**Best for:** Microsoft 365 organizations with many report viewers and someone who can watch Fabric capacity metrics. **Not ideal for:** unpredictable spikes on a small capacity, or teams that want warehouse-native live queries without modeling.


- **Pricing:** Pro is $14 and Premium Per User $24 per user per month, paid yearly. Viewers need a paid license unless content sits on Fabric F64 or Premium P1 capacity or larger ([Power BI pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ). Fabric capacity is billed per capacity unit (CU) hour, pay-as-you-go or reserved ([Fabric pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/microsoft-fabric/) ). 60-day Fabric trial. Verified November 2026.
- **Under load:** Fabric “smooths interactive operations over a minimum of five minutes, and up to 64 minutes,” and background operations over 24 hours ([throttling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/enterprise/throttling) ). Past 10 minutes of future usage, interactive requests get 20-second delays, and past an hour they’re rejected. Overage billing avoids throttling but “costs three times the normal capacity rate,” and admins can cap paid overage per 24 hours.
- **DirectQuery limits:** concurrent DirectQuery connections per semantic model are 5 on F2, 50 on F64, and 200 on F512 and above ([capacity limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/enterprise/powerbi/service-premium-what-is) ). Import mode is the default and runs on Power BI’s in-memory engine;[query caching](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/power-bi-query-caching) is Premium and Embedded only and off by default.
- **Security:**[DAX row-level security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security) on Import, DirectQuery, and Direct Lake models. Sign-in and provisioning run through Microsoft Entra ID.
- **AI:**[Copilot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/copilot-introduction) needs paid Fabric F2 or higher or Premium P1; a Pro or PPU license alone isn’t enough.
- **Embedding:** Power BI Embedded A SKUs and Fabric F SKUs, both billed by the hour.


## Amazon Quick Sight: best for large, spiky audiences on AWS


**Best for:** AWS customers with many occasional viewers, including embedded dashboards in a SaaS app. **Not ideal for:** live queries that run longer than two minutes, or teams outside AWS.


- **Pricing:** Reader $3 and Author $24 per user per month; Reader Pro $20 and Author Pro $40 add generative AI. A $250 per month account fee applies once you have a Pro user or Q&A enabled. SPICE costs $0.38 per GB per month beyond 10 GB included per Author ([Quick Sight pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/quicksight/pricing/) ). Verified November 2026.
- **Session pricing for spikes:** capacity pricing sells 30-minute reader sessions: 500 for $250 per month plus $0.50 per extra session, falling to $0.16 per extra session at 1.6 million sessions a year, aimed at “embedded applications or large-scale BI deployments.”
- **Under load:** SPICE is an “in-memory data store engineered to scale automatically,” so dashboards on SPICE don’t hit your database during a spike. Direct queries time out after two minutes ([data source limits](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/data-source-limits.html) ). Enterprise edition allows hourly SPICE refreshes and incremental refreshes every 15 minutes ([refresh options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/refreshing-imported-data.html) ).
- **Security:** row-level security on Enterprise edition, SAML 2.0 identity providers, and SCIM provisioning through IAM Identity Center.
- **AI:** Author Pro builds dashboards from natural language, creates Q topics, and writes executive summaries and data stories.
- **Embedding:** 1-click embedding and API embedding on Enterprise edition ([embedding overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/embedding-overview.html) ).


## ThoughtSpot: best for search-style AI on a live warehouse


**Best for:** organizations that want business users asking questions in natural language against Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks, with a usage-based option. **Not ideal for:** teams that need the BI tool to cache or throttle load for them.


- **Pricing:** Essentials is $25 per user per month (5 to 50 users, up to 25 million rows) and Pro $50 per user per month (up to 1,000 users and 250 million rows, with 25 Spotter queries per user per month), both billed annually. A usage-based Pro plan starts at $0.10 per credit ([ThoughtSpot pricing](https://www.thoughtspot.com/pricing) ), and “one credit is consumed for every query that is generated” in most cases ([consumption pricing](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/software/26.9.0.sw/consumption-pricing-query-based) ). Free trial available. Verified November 2026.
- **Under load:** “ThoughtSpot does not cache linked data” and queries the external database directly ([Snowflake connection](https://docs.thoughtspot.com/cloud/26.11.0.cl/connections-snowflake-add) ). ThoughtSpot “may generate large numbers of concurrent queries” and documents no limit of its own. The in-memory Spotcache is an add-on.
- **Security:** row-level security on every plan; SAML, OAuth, and OIDC single sign-on on Pro and Enterprise; SCIM is enabled by default.
- **AI:** Spotter, an AI analyst; ThoughtSpot “does not meter or charge for LLM tokens.”
- **Embedding:** the Visual Embed SDK, including a Spotter component, and REST API v2.


## Tableau Cloud: best for extract-heavy dashboards with predictable traffic


**Best for:** analyst teams already standardized on Tableau whose dashboards can run on extracts. **Not ideal for:** sudden audience spikes on live dashboards, or teams that want AI on the base edition.


- **Pricing:** Standard starts at $15 and Enterprise at $35 per user per month, billed annually; Cloud+ adds Tableau Agent at an unpublished price ([Tableau pricing](https://www.tableau.com/pricing/teams-orgs) ). Capacity-based viewer blocks are available “with no overage charges” through sales. 14-day trial. Verified November 2026.
- **Under load:** Tableau Cloud publishes[site capacity limits](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/to_site_capacity.htm) : up to 600 view requests per hour per user, 40 GB of query memory, and 15 concurrent extract refresh jobs on Standard, 25 on Enterprise, and 50 on Cloud+ and Tableau+, with eight backgrounder hours per Creator license per day. “Requests beyond the allowed limit might be rejected.”
- **Caching:** for live connections, “Tableau Cloud refreshes cached data every 12 hours by default,” and a workbook set to “Always live” sends every view to the database ([data freshness](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/data_freshness_policy.htm) ).
- **Security:** user filters on any edition, data policies with Data Management, SAML or OIDC, and[SCIM](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/scim_config_online.htm) .
- **AI:** Pulse is in Standard. Tableau Agent is listed under Cloud+ on the pricing page, while the[help docs](https://help.tableau.com/current/online/en-us/web_author_einstein.htm) say it requires Tableau+.
- **Embedding:** Embedding API v3 web components with JWT; embedded viewers can be licensed by analytical impressions.


## Metabase: best for self-hosted teams that scale their own servers


**Best for:** startups and mid-size teams that want an open-source option and are comfortable running more app servers as usage grows. **Not ideal for:** teams that need caching or row-level security without paying for Pro.


- **Pricing:** open source is free. Starter is $100 per month for 5 users plus $6 per extra user; Pro is $575 per month for 10 users plus $12 per extra user; Enterprise starts at $20,000 per year ([Metabase pricing](https://www.metabase.com/pricing/) ). 14-day trial. Verified November 2026.
- **Under load:** Metabase scales horizontally by running more instances against the same application database behind a load balancer, and suggests roughly “1 CPU core and 1GB of RAM” for every 20 concurrent users ([Metabase at scale](https://www.metabase.com/learn/metabase-basics/administration/administration-and-operation/metabase-at-scale) ). Queries time out after 20 minutes by default.
- **Caching:** duration and schedule[caching policies](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/configuring-metabase/caching) are Pro and Enterprise only.[Model persistence](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/data-modeling/model-persistence) works on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Redshift and doesn’t work with row and column security.
- **Security:** row and column security, SAML, and SCIM are Pro and Enterprise only.
- **AI:**[Metabot](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/ai/metabot) creates charts from natural language and generates SQL on every plan. Metabase’s managed AI costs $3.75 per million tokens after 1 million free, or you bring your own key.
- **Embedding:** guest embeds on every plan; the modular embedding SDK and full-app embedding on Pro and Enterprise.


## Basedash: best for small data teams that want AI answers on live data at a flat price


**Best for:** startups and mid-size companies that want an AI data analyst on Postgres, Snowflake, BigQuery, or ClickHouse with a predictable monthly bill. **Not ideal for:** large viewer counts on one plan, warehouses that can’t scale on their own, or teams that need the BI tool to queue and throttle query load.


- **Pricing:** Startup is $1,000 per month plus AI usage for up to 25 users, including $1,000 per month in AI credits; overage is charged on the next bill. Enterprise is custom ([Basedash pricing](https://www.basedash.com/pricing) ). 14-day free trial, no card. Verified November 2026.
- **Under load:** Basedash queries your[connected database or warehouse](https://www.basedash.com/docs/data-sources/introduction) live, so its elasticity is your warehouse’s. Queries return up to 10,000 rows, and Postgres queries time out after about two minutes, adjustable per data source ([SQL editor](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/sql-editor) ). Self-hosted, one Docker Compose server covers about 500 users ([self-hosting](https://www.basedash.com/docs/self-hosting/overview) ).
- **Caching:**[query caching](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/organization-settings) is on by default; charts load from cache and refresh in the background, which speeds up loads rather than removing the warehouse query.[Dashboards](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/dashboards) refresh every 15 minutes while open and not at all while closed. The managed[Basedash Warehouse](https://www.basedash.com/features/warehouse) can take heavy reporting off a production database.
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/row-level-security) is Postgres and Supabase only. SAML or OIDC[SSO](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/sso) and SCIM are Enterprise features.
- **AI and embedding:** the[AI data analyst](https://www.basedash.com/features/ai-data-analyst) writes SQL against live data and builds dashboards from a prompt on every plan.[Embedding](https://www.basedash.com/docs/developers/embedding) through iframes and a React SDK is Enterprise only.
- **Tradeoff:** Basedash has no documented concurrency queue or capacity controls, so a spike reaches your warehouse directly. Looker’s connection caps or Databricks’ dashboard cache give more control.


## Which BI tool should you choose for query spikes?


**You want elastic scaling during peak queries on Snowflake, with no-SQL users.** Sigma and ThoughtSpot both query Snowflake live and let business users explore without SQL, so turn on multi-cluster auto-scale (Enterprise Edition) and they inherit it. Basedash fits smaller teams that prefer plain-English questions.


**You embed charts in a SaaS app and traffic spikes at month end.** Quick Sight’s session pricing and SPICE are built for this audience pattern. Databricks AI/BI embedding with its 24-hour cache suits lakehouse teams. Power BI Embedded works if you size the A or F SKU for the peak. Our[embedded analytics pricing comparison](https://www.basedash.com/blog/embedded-analytics-pricing-compared-2026) covers per-session and per-tenant models in detail.


**You need to cap warehouse spend, not just survive the spike.** Looker’s connection limit, Databricks’ cluster maximum, and Power BI’s capacity size all cap concurrent compute. ThoughtSpot and Basedash rely on warehouse-side limits such as Snowflake’s maximum cluster count.


**Your team is growing from 10 to 500 users.** Per-user plans (Power BI, Tableau, ThoughtSpot) grow linearly with seats. Databricks AI/BI charges no seat fee, Quick Sight readers start at $3, and self-hosted Metabase only grows with your servers. Basedash’s Startup plan stops at 25 users, so larger rollouts go to Enterprise.


**You want usage-based pricing that tracks query volume.** ThoughtSpot’s credit plan, Databricks DBUs, and Quick Sight sessions all bill by use. Our[guide to usage-based BI pricing](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-tools-with-usage-based-pricing-2026) compares what each one meters.


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the best BI tools that scale elastically with query spikes?


Databricks AI/BI, Sigma, and Looker handle spikes best when paired with an autoscaling warehouse, because every query runs in compute that can add clusters on demand. Databricks serverless SQL warehouses queue queries while the autoscaler adds clusters, and Sigma and Looker push queries to Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift. Power BI and Amazon Quick Sight absorb spikes in their own engines instead: Power BI through Fabric capacity smoothing and optional overage billing, Quick Sight through its SPICE in-memory store, which AWS says scales automatically.


### Which BI tools can scale as query volume grows without massive cost increases?


Caching is the biggest lever. Databricks dashboards serve a 24-hour result cache without starting the SQL warehouse, Looker caches for an hour by default and can match caches to ETL with datagroups, and Sigma materializations write heavy datasets back to the warehouse as tables. Pricing models matter too: Quick Sight reader sessions fall to $0.16 each at high annual volume, and self-hosted Metabase has no license cost. Tools that send every view to the warehouse, like ThoughtSpot’s linked data, depend on warehouse settings to control cost.


### How do I estimate the cost of a BI tool that handles about 500 concurrent queries?


Split the estimate into the BI license and the compute that runs the queries. For live-query tools, compute is your warehouse: Databricks recommends one SQL warehouse cluster per 10 concurrent queries, so 500 concurrent queries implies roughly 50 clusters at peak. On BigQuery on-demand, a project gets up to 2,000 concurrent slots and pays $6.25 per TiB scanned. For Power BI, check that your Fabric SKU’s DirectQuery connection cap (200 per model at F512 and above) and capacity units cover the peak, or budget for overage at three times the normal rate.


### Which dashboard tools can auto-refresh every five minutes without performance problems?


Basedash dashboards can refresh every 1, 5, or 15 minutes while open and stop refreshing when closed, which limits load to dashboards people are actually viewing. Power BI DirectQuery dashboards can refresh tiles as often as every 15 minutes, with faster automatic page refresh on Premium and Fabric capacity. Tableau Cloud extracts refresh hourly at most, so five-minute refresh needs a live connection set to “Always live.” On a popular dashboard, five-minute refresh multiplies warehouse queries, so pair it with warehouse autoscaling.


### What happens when a Power BI Fabric capacity is overloaded?


Fabric smooths interactive usage over five to 64 minutes and background jobs over 24 hours. If you’ve already consumed the next 10 minutes of capacity, interactive operations get 20-second delays. Beyond one hour of future usage, new interactive requests are rejected, and beyond 24 hours every new request is rejected. You can avoid throttling by enabling capacity overage, billed at three times the normal rate with an optional 24-hour spending cap, or by moving to a larger F SKU.


### Which BI tools with AI assistants work for about 50 analysts on usage-based pricing?


ThoughtSpot’s usage-based Pro plan starts at $0.10 per credit, includes Spotter, and doesn’t meter LLM tokens. Databricks AI/BI has no license fee, and Genie is free for users until January 31, 2027, with SQL compute billed separately. Looker Conversational Analytics bills tokens from February 1, 2027. Basedash’s Startup plan covers up to 25 users, so 50 analysts would need Enterprise.
